title: Felementum
summary: An interactive 3D explorer for N-tier supply chain networks that follows materials from OEMs down to the mines, for spotting systemic suppliers and single-country dependencies.

narrative.problem: Supply chains run many tiers deep, from finished products through module integrators, component makers and refiners to extraction sites, so systemic suppliers, single-country dependencies and hidden concentration risk are hard to see from any single tier.
narrative.decision: Runs entirely in the browser as a static site on seeded synthetic data, with an optional data assistant that works locally or with the visitor's own AI provider key, held only in browser memory.
narrative.tradeoff: No real supplier data is shown, so concentration and exposure figures demonstrate the method rather than describe any company, and larger datasets must be downloaded to the browser (about 6 MB for the stress set).
narrative.limitation: Company names and supplier relationships are fictional and mine capacities approximate; the 68 Playwright checks test the interface, and no validation of the risk measures against real supply chains is reported.
narrative.caveat: Synthetic data: company names and supplier relationships are fictional. Mine sites are real public locations, but their capacities are approximate and for illustration only; nothing describes any real company's supply chain.
